profile.summary: scCello is a transcriptome foundation model for single-cell RNA-seq data. It reads a cell as a list of genes ordered by expression and outputs a cell representation (and masked-gene predictions). During pre-training it also uses each cell's cell-type label and the cell ontology graph, so that cells of the same or related types end up close together.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: scCello is a stack of transformer encoder layers. Each cell's genes are normalised and ranked by expression (rank value encoding, taken from Geneformer) and fed in as a sequence of gene tokens. Pre-training minimises four losses together: masked gene prediction as in BERT, an intra-cellular cell-type coherence loss that pulls cells of the same type together, an inter-cellular relational alignment loss that uses similarities between cell types computed on the cell ontology graph, and a regularisation term.

quotes.text: scCello utilizes a stack of self-attention transformer encoder layers [63]
we employ Rank Value Encoding [61] approach to rank genes based on their normalized expression set
Same as BERT [15], scCello predicts a randomly masked gene token in each cell based on its surrounding context in the sequence.
an ontologybased cell-type coherence loss to encourage cell representations of the same cell type to aggregate
a relational alignment loss to guide the cell representation learning by consulting the cell-type lineage from the cell ontology graph
θ∗ ← arg min LMGP + LInter + LIntra + LReg

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The README names one pre-trained checkpoint on Hugging Face, katarinayuan/scCello-zeroshot. The README loads the same checkpoint both for zero-shot use and, with a classification head, for linear probing. The checkpoint repository holds config.json and pytorch_model.bin and no model card. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision, and the repository commit used to run it.

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: The authors evaluate scCello on cell type clustering and batch integration, cell type classification, classification of novel cell types, marker gene prediction and cancer drug response prediction. The repository has one script per task.

quotes.text: The `sccello/script` folder contains all executable files.
identifying novel cell types of unseen cells, prediction of cell-type-specific marker genes, and cancer drug responses

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Transcriptome foundation model for single-cell RNA-seq, pre-trained with cell ontology guidance.

quotes.text: a cell-ontology guided transcriptome foundation model (TFM) for single cell RNA-seq data

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: BERT-style transformer encoder: 6 layers, hidden size 256, 4 attention heads, intermediate size 512, ReLU activation (released config).

quotes.text: scCello utilizes a stack of self-attention transformer encoder layers [63]

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A single-cell gene expression profile, normalised and turned into a sequence of gene tokens ordered by expression rank. The repository converts h5ad files to the Hugging Face dataset format.
facts.source_locator: arXiv Section 2.1 and Appendix D; README.md: h5ad Data Format Transformation

quotes.text: Each single-cell transcriptome is represented by a sequence of tuples, each containing genes and their expression counts.
Each sequence was then ordered by the rank of the gene expression values [61]
Example data for transforming h5ad format to huggingface format.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Cell representations (the paper's comparison table lists CLS for scCello) and masked gene token predictions; with a classification head, cell type labels.
facts.source_locator: arXiv Sections 2.2 and Table 9; README.md: Model Checkpoints

quotes.text: scCello predicts a randomly masked gene token in each cell based on its surrounding context in the sequence

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: 22 million cells from human h5ad data downloaded from the CellxGene database, with cell-type labels mapped to the Cell Ontology from the OBO Foundry. The pre-training set is published on Hugging Face as katarinayuan/scCello_pretrain_unsplitted.

quotes.text: we downloaded a series of human h5ad data from [CellxGene]
We pre-trained scCello on 22 million cells from CellxGene database leveraging their cell-type labels mapped to the cell ontology graph from Open Biological and Biomedical Ontology Foundry.

strengths.text: Uses cell-type labels and the cell ontology during pre-training, not only masked gene prediction.

quotes.text: We introduce cell-type coherence loss and ontology alignment loss, which are minimized along with the masked gene expression prediction loss during the pre-training.

strengths.text: Small model: about 10.7 million parameters, against 674,745,857 for UCE in the authors' own comparison table.

quotes.text: Configuration Geneformer [61] scGPT [14] scTab [19] UCE [55] scCello #Parameters

strengths.text: Code, weights and the pre-training dataset are all public, with a script for each downstream task.

quotes.text: Source code and model weights are available at https://github.com/DeepGraphLearning/scCello.

limitations.text: The authors note that the cell ontology keeps changing and that updating the model to a new ontology currently means retraining it.

quotes.text: The cell ontology is constantly revised and expanded. In the future, we plan to investigate more efficient methods for fine-tuning scCello to enable continual learning of updated ontology, rather than retraining the entire model.

run_guide.summary: Clone the repository, install the dependencies and load the released scCello checkpoint from Hugging Face.
prerequisites: Conda and pip. The README states PyTorch 2.0 and Python 3.9.
The installation installs PyTorch with pytorch-cuda=11.7 and the RAPIDS libraries cupy, cuml and cugraph. GPU needs are not otherwise stated.
Internet access to download katarinayuan/scCello-zeroshot from Hugging Face.
